data.body:
Scoped Defect-2 final report (paging gap only). I did not implement Defect 1 and I am not closing this ticket because AC3-AC6 / ceiling work remain unresolved by scope.

## Defect 2 RCA

Terraform-managed: YES.

Source of truth:
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf`: `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.root_disk_pressure` / live alarm `rebar-root-disk-pressure`, metric `rebar/host:root_disk_used_percent`, SNS `alarm_actions` and `ok_actions` wired to `aws_sns_topic.alerts`.
- `infra/terraform/monitoring.tf`: `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.gerrit_data_disk_high` / live alarm `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high`, metric `rebar/host:disk_used_percent` for `mount=/var/gerrit`, same SNS wiring.

Root cause: both host-published disk alarms had `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`. For metrics emitted by the failing host, publisher silence is not evidence of health; it is a dead-man signal. Live `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` confirmed both disk alarms were still `TreatMissingData=notBreaching` before the fix. The same live read confirmed the alarm actions point at `arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:896586841071:rebar-gerrit-alerts`, and `aws sns list-subscriptions-by-topic` showed a confirmed email subscription to `joeoakhart@navapbc.com`.

Discriminating proof: the outage metric gap had no `root_disk_used_percent` or `GerritReachable` datapoints from ~2026-09-02 01:40 PDT to 07:10 PDT. CloudWatch history for `rebar-root-disk-pressure` showed ALARM -> OK at 01:45 PDT under the old disk alarm semantics. By contrast, `rebar-gerrit-gate-down` already uses `TreatMissingData=breaching` and moved OK -> ALARM at 02:05 with reason `no datapoints were received for 2 periods and 2 missing datapoints were treated as [Breaching]`. Alarm action history for both `rebar-gerrit-gate-down` and `rebar-root-disk-pressure` shows successful SNS executions, so the broken artifact was missing-data classification, not SNS wiring.

Defect origins for this scoped defect:
- root disk alarm: commit `7ed670b0342db0132ea7d41fe8a013cdc386cedf` (`rebar-ticket: ac14-363f-4ba0-4b5c`) introduced `notBreaching` with the incorrect "gate-down already pages, don't double-page" assumption.
- data disk alarm: commit `5e1a59491f2ea5c7de55c6d7db972d8207acddcc` (`rebar-ticket: c7d4`) copied the same assumption.
This ticket remains open/in_progress, so I did not close with a single `--caused-by`; the attribution is recorded here.

## Fix landed

Gerrit change: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2523
Merged SHA: `8bf0101dc1b441c894c704334a6c1ae588d4ecc7`
Votes before submit: `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, unresolved comments `0`.
CI_RESULT: `{ "run_id": "33660725511", "status": "passed", "duration_seconds": 1725, "fixes_applied": [], "retry_count": 0 }`

Code change:
- `rebar-root-disk-pressure`: `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`.
- `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high`: `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`.
- Existing Terraform alarm guard extended with `test_host_published_disk_alarms_treat_missing_data_as_breaching`, which fails if either disk alarm goes back to missing-data-as-healthy.

Local verification:
- RED first: `pytest tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py::test_host_published_disk_alarms_treat_missing_data_as_breaching -q` failed against current main because both alarms were `notBreaching`.
- GREEN: full `pytest tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py -q` passed (6 tests).
- Mutation teeth: sandboxed mutation reintroduced `notBreaching` on the two disk alarms and the held-out test returned RED.
- `make lint` passed.
- `terraform -chdir=infra/terraform init -backend=false -input=false` + `terraform validate` passed.
- `terraform plan -lock=false -input=false -no-color -detailed-exitcode` returned exit 2 and showed exactly the two intended alarm diffs `notBreaching -> breaching`, plus an unrelated existing drift: `aws_instance.gerrit root_block_device.volume_size 60 -> 30`.

Important live-state note: I did NOT apply Terraform or mutate AWS. Live `describe-alarms` will remain `notBreaching` until an operator applies this Terraform change. A full unqualified apply currently also sees the manual recovery drift trying to reconcile root volume size `60 -> 30`; do not blindly apply until that root-volume drift is consciously handled, or use a human-approved targeted alarm apply. That is outside my Defect-2 code scope and overlaps the Defect-1 sizing/design constraint.

## Defect 1 standing-intent summary + recommendation

Standing intent from related tickets/docs: root disk pressure is to be caught early and remediated by bounded, measured reclaim without destroying rollback lifelines or Gerrit data. ADR 0012 deliberately keeps Gerrit state on a separate `/var/gerrit` gp3 data volume with `prevent_destroy`; root holds Docker images/layers/build cache, nginx temp, and review-bot temp/snapshot work. The runbook says root-disk pressure is primarily recovered by Docker builder/image prune and clearing root-temp review/snapshot caches, then rerunning affected reviews.

What has already been tried:
- `sour-plugugly-rhino` / `28f9-535c-ce9c-4583`: added pressure-triggered Docker prune on the autodeploy no-op tick so quiescent main still reclaims.
- `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` / `3a52-2d79-320d-4fed`: proved later pressure was not just deploy-timing; snapshot janitor thresholds were disk-size-blind/unreachable on 30 GiB root, spawning byte-cap follow-up `3907-0110-7688-43bd`.
- `besotted-witty-murrelet` / `e4f3-1661-2319-4a76`: identified MCP blue-green tagged images/insufficient image retirement as a new persistent root consumer.
- `preodorous-temporary-piglet` / `3cef-c948-68ba-40fd`: added acute pressure behavior: at hard pressure, prune build cache without the 5 GiB keep floor and add low-disk review admission so reviews defer instead of fail-closing.
- This ticket's AC3 measurement shows a broader ceiling problem remains: `/var/lib/docker` 17 GiB / `overlay2` 16 GiB with ~6.5 GiB orphaned layer state invisible to normal prune, `/var/tmp` 3.6 GiB, journald 1.7 GiB, and ~4.8 GiB container writable layers with 0 reclaimable by `docker system df`.

Recommendation to orchestrator: split Defect 1 into a separate design-reviewed infra story/epic (or keep this ticket in_progress for that owner) whose scope is an explicit root-working-set ceiling across all observed accumulators: Docker orphan/overlay2 and writable-layer lifecycle, `/var/tmp` retention, journald `SystemMaxUse`, and the already-open `/var/gerrit` follow-up `scowlful-bovine-dragonfly`. Do not accept another "run prune earlier" mitigation as satisfying AC4; the evidence says normal prune can miss most of the 29 GiB working set. Also reconcile the live 60 GiB recovery resize with Terraform state/config before any broad infra apply.

Ticket state after this scoped pass: `cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin` remains `in_progress`; no AC boxes were changed and no close attempted.
